donorPrimitiveClaims: known causal ancestry and operator semantics make much of uninformed intervention enumeration unnecessary
different names or formulas can denote behaviorally equivalent mechanisms and would otherwise create false novelty

hypothesis: Behaviorally equivalent causal subgraphs with different syntax can be crystallized into one reusable semantic operator, and using that operator during backward causal compilation can reduce symbolic goal expansion on held-out syntactic variants without changing exact minimum interventions.

mechanism.training: Compute exact Boolean boundary truth tables for multiple syntactically distinct implementations of the same causal function and crystallize only signatures observed in at least two distinct graph structures.
mechanism.admission: A held-out causal subgraph may use a crystal only when its complete declared Boolean boundary truth table exactly matches the crystal signature.
mechanism.use: Backward goal compilation may solve the crystal truth table over boundary inputs instead of recursively expanding the internal subgraph.
mechanism.fallback: If no exact semantic crystal matches or safe tree-like applicability conditions fail, use the existing exact causal compiler.

heldOutSyntaxes: NOT(XNOR(A,B)) implemented as NOT(NOT(XOR(A,B))) for XOR2
NOT(OR(NOT(A),NOT(B))) wrapped through COPY for AND2
NOT(AND(NOT(A),NOT(B))) wrapped through COPY for OR2
nested target graphs where a held-out semantic motif feeds AND/OR/XOR with additional controllable leaves
negativeControls: a unique 3-input majority function must not be admitted as a 2-input crystal
falsifier: Any crystal maps two different declared truth tables to one semantic identity.
Any held-out case changes satisfiability or minimum intervention cardinality versus exhaustive search.
Any negative control is admitted to the wrong crystal.
Median symbolic goal-state expansion reduction is below 30 percent.
A crystal is admitted from syntax alone without exact boundary behavior verification.
promotionBoundary: A pass supports only a narrow semantic-causal-macro child mechanism. It does not prove general causal abstraction, causal discovery, or transfer beyond declared Boolean SCMs.
